html:
Seven stone posts carved with Sanskrit verses, set up around 400 CE at Muara Kaman on the Mahakam River in East Kalimantan, Borneo. They are the oldest written records found in Indonesia.

A yupa is a sacrificial post from Vedic ritual. The texts, in Sanskrit and a southern Indian script related to the Pallava script, praise King Mulavarman of the kingdom later called Kutai Martadipura. They name his father Aswawarman and his grandfather Kudungga. Kudungga has a local, not an Indian, name, which suggests a local family that took up Indian ways.

The inscriptions record Mulavarman's gifts to brahmins, including thousands of cattle and gold. Almost nothing else is known of his kingdom. Together with the slightly later inscriptions of Tarumanagara in west Java, they show Indian religion and kingship reaching the islands along the sea trade, centuries before Srivijaya.
sum: Seven stone posts carved with Sanskrit verses, set up around 400 CE at Muara Kaman on the Mahakam River in East Kalimantan, Borneo. They are the oldest written records found in Indonesia.
